from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler

# Copy the datasets to avoid modifying the original data
train_df_processed = train_df_copy.copy()
test_df_processed = test_df_copy.copy()

# Handling missing values (if any)
train_df_processed.fillna(train_df_processed.mean(), inplace=True)
test_df_processed.fillna(test_df_processed.mean(), inplace=True)

# Encoding categorical variables
label_encoder = LabelEncoder()
for column in ['month', 'day']:
    train_df_processed[column] = label_encoder.fit_transform(train_df_processed[column])
    test_df_processed[column] = label_encoder.transform(test_df_processed[column])

# Scaling numerical features (excluding the label column 'area')
scaler = StandardScaler()
numeric_features = ['X', 'Y', 'FFMC', 'DMC', 'DC', 'ISI', 'temp', 'RH', 'wind', 'rain']
train_df_processed[numeric_features] = scaler.fit_transform(train_df_processed[numeric_features])
test_df_processed[numeric_features] = scaler.transform(test_df_processed[numeric_features])

# Display the first few rows of the processed datasets
print("Processed Training Data:")
print(train_df_processed.head())
print("\nProcessed Testing Data:")
print(test_df_processed.head())

code:
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

# Identify categorical and numerical columns
categorical_cols = ['month', 'day']
numerical_cols = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in categorical_cols and col != 'area']

# Define preprocessing for numerical data
numerical_transformer = StandardScaler()

# Define preprocessing for categorical data
categorical_transformer = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore')

# Bundle preprocessing for numerical and categorical data
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ('num', numerical_transformer, numerical_cols),
        ('cat', categorical_transformer, categorical_cols)
    ])

# Create a pipeline that applies the preprocessing steps
pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[('preprocessor', preprocessor)])

# Fit and transform the training data
train_df_processed = pipeline.fit_transform(train_df_copy)

# Transform the testing data
test_df_processed = pipeline.transform(test_df_copy)

# Display the processed data shapes
print(f"Processed Training Data Shape: {train_df_processed.shape}")
print(f"Processed Testing Data Shape: {test_df_processed.shape}")
execute_result:
Processed Training Data Shape: (413, 29)
Processed Testing Data Shape: (104, 29)

# Splitting the preprocessed data into features (X) and target variable (y) for both training and testing sets
# Copying the processed data to avoid modifying the original processed data
train_df_processed_copy = train_df_processed.copy()
test_df_processed_copy = test_df_processed.copy()

# The last column is assumed to be the target variable 'area'
# Dropping the last column to get the features
X_train = train_df_processed_copy[:, :-1]
X_test = test_df_processed_copy[:, :-1]

# Extracting the last column as the target variable
y_train = train_df_processed_copy[:, -1]
y_test = test_df_processed_copy[:, -1]

# Printing the shapes to verify the split
print(f"Shape of X_train: {X_train.shape}")
print(f"Shape of y_train: {y_train.shape}")
print(f"Shape of X_test: {X_test.shape}")
print(f"Shape of y_test: {y_test.shape}")

code:
from xgboost import XGBRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, r2_score

# Initialize the XGBoost model with some hyperparameters
model = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=1000,
    max_depth=7,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    subsample=0.8,
    colsample_bytree=0.8,
    random_state=42
)

# Train the model
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predict on the training set to evaluate the model
y_train_pred = model.predict(X_train)
train_rmse = mean_squared_error(y_train, y_train_pred, squared=False)
train_r2 = r2_score(y_train, y_train_pred)

# Predict on the testing set to evaluate the model
y_test_pred = model.predict(X_test)
test_rmse = mean_squared_error(y_test, y_test_pred, squared=False)
test_r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_test_pred)

# Print the evaluation metrics
print(f"Training RMSE: {train_rmse:.4f}, R2 Score: {train_r2:.4f}")
print(f"Testing RMSE: {test_rmse:.4f}, R2 Score: {test_r2:.4f}")
